```{ojs}
  283.6,42,66.2,25.5,  232.1,8.6,8.7,13.4

rgAd = Array.from({length: rgRaw.length / 4}, (_, i) =>
  ({TV: rgRaw[4 * i], Radio: rgRaw[4 * i + 1], Newspaper: rgRaw[4 * i + 2], Sales: rgRaw[4 * i + 3]}))
rgMean = a => a.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / a.length
// Simple least squares and every quantity of ISLR 3.1 from two columns.
// Checked against R's lm(), summary() and confint() to 4 decimals.
rgSimple = (x, y) => {
  const n = x.length, mx = rgMean(x), my = rgMean(y);
  let sxy = 0, sxx = 0, syy = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const dx = x[i] - mx, dy = y[i] - my; sxy += dx * dy; sxx += dx * dx; syy += dy * dy; }
  const b1 = sxy / sxx, b0 = my - b1 * mx, rss = syy - b1 * sxy, rse = Math.sqrt(rss / (n - 2)), se1 = rse / Math.sqrt(sxx);
  return {n, mx, my, sxy, sxx, b0, b1, rss, tss: syy, rse, se1, t1: b1 / se1,
          r: sxy / Math.sqrt(sxx * syy), r2: 1 - rss / syy, adj: 1 - (rss / (n - 2)) / (syy / (n - 1))};
}
// Multiple least squares (ISLR 3.2): the normal equations, inverted by
// Gauss-Jordan, so the standard errors come from the same inverse.
rgOls = names => {
  const n = rgAd.length, k = names.length + 1, y = rgAd.map(d => d.Sales);
  const X = rgAd.map(d => [1, ...names.map(v => d[v])]);
  const A = Array.from({length: k}, (_, i) => [
    ...Array.from({length: k}, (_, j) => X.reduce((s, row) => s + row[i] * row[j], 0)),
    ...Array.from({length: k}, (_, j) => +(i === j))]);
  for (let c = 0; c < k; c++) {
    let piv = c;
    for (let r = c + 1; r < k; r++) if (Math.abs(A[r][c]) > Math.abs(A[piv][c])) piv = r;
    [A[c], A[piv]] = [A[piv], A[c]];
    const d = A[c][c];
    for (let j = 0; j < 2 * k; j++) A[c][j] /= d;
    for (let r = 0; r < k; r++) if (r !== c) { const f = A[r][c]; for (let j = 0; j < 2 * k; j++) A[r][j] -= f * A[c][j]; }
  }
  const inv = A.map(row => row.slice(k));
  const xty = Array.from({length: k}, (_, i) => X.reduce((s, row, m) => s + row[i] * y[m], 0));
  const b = inv.map(row => row.reduce((s, v, j) => s + v * xty[j], 0));
  const my = rgMean(y), df = n - k;
  const rss = X.reduce((s, row, m) => s + (y[m] - row.reduce((a, v, j) => a + v * b[j], 0)) ** 2, 0);
  const tss = y.reduce((s, v) => s + (v - my) ** 2, 0), s2 = rss / df;
  const se = inv.map((row, i) => Math.sqrt(s2 * row[i]));
  return {names: ["Intercept", ...names], b, se, t: b.map((v, i) => v / se[i]), n, k, df, rss, tss,
          rse: Math.sqrt(s2), r2: 1 - rss / tss, adj: 1 - (rss / df) / (tss / (n - 1)), F: ((tss - rss) / (k - 1)) / s2};
}
// p-values from the exact t and F distributions (clTcdf, clIbeta: section 05).
rgP2 = (t, df) => 2 * clTcdf(-Math.abs(t), df)
rgFp = (F, d1, d2) => clIbeta(d2 / 2, d1 / 2, d2 / (d2 + d1 * F))
rgPfmt = p => p < 0.0001 ? "< 0.0001" : p.toFixed(4)
rgPeq = p => `p ${p < 0.0001 ? "" : "= "}${rgPfmt(p)}`
rgN = (v, k = 4) => v.toLocaleString("en-GB", {minimumFractionDigits: k, maximumFractionDigits: k}).replace("-", "−")
// A negative factor in a product goes in brackets: "6.47 − (−0.56) × 7.47".
rgNp = (v, k = 4) => v < 0 ? `(${rgN(v, k)})` : rgN(v, k)
rgCol = name => rgAd.map(d => d[name])
rgTV = rgSimple(rgCol("TV"), rgCol("Sales"))
rgStyle = ({fontSize: "14px", fontFamily: "Roboto, sans-serif", color: PPAL.soft, background: "transparent"})
rgTitle = s => Plot.text([s], {frameAnchor: "top-left", dy: -30, text: d => d, fill: PPAL.navy, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 6, fontWeight: 700, fontSize: 16})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const fit = rgSimple(rgCol(rgSx), rgCol("Sales")), hi = d3.max(rgCol(rgSx));
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: 1000, height: 280, marginLeft: 40, marginBottom: 28, marginTop: 42, style: rgStyle,
    x: {domain: [0, hi * 1.02], label: null, tickSize: 4},
    y: {domain: [0, 28], label: null, ticks: [0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25], tickSize: 4},
    marks: [
      Plot.dot(rgAd, {x: rgSx, y: "Sales", r: 3.5, fill: PPAL.soft, fillOpacity: 0.5}),
      Plot.line([0, hi], {x: d => d, y: d => fit.b0 + fit.b1 * d, stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeWidth: 3}),
      rgTitle(`Sales (1000s of units) against the ${rgSx} budget ($1000s)`)
    ]
  });
  const pct = v => `${(100 * v).toFixed(1)}%`;
  const say = rgSx === "Newspaper"
    ? `Newspaper is the weakest link: r = ${rgN(fit.r, 3)}, so the line explains only <b>${pct(fit.r2)}</b> of the variation in sales. Yet its slope is positive. Does newspaper advertising sell, or does it ride along with radio? The last slide of this section settles it.`
    : `${rgSx} has r = ${rgN(fit.r, 3)}, so the line explains <b>R² = r² = ${pct(fit.r2)}</b> of the variation in sales. Each extra $1,000 on ${rgSx === "TV" ? "TV" : "radio"} goes with about <b>${(1000 * fit.b1).toFixed(1)} more units</b> sold.`;
  return html`${chart}
  <div class="ojs-eq rg-stats">
    <span>Sales = ${rgN(fit.b0)} + ${rgN(fit.b1)} × ${rgSx}</span>
    <span>r = <span class="cl-navy">${rgN(fit.r, 3)}</span></span>
    <span>R² = ${rgN(fit.r2, 3)}</span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb">${say}</div>`;
}
```

## Is the Correlation Real? {.ojs-slide #cor-test}

::: {.lede-min}
Under $H_0\colon \rho = 0$, $t = r\sqrt{n-2}\,/\sqrt{1-r^2}$ follows Student's $t$ with $n-2$ degrees of freedom. The defaults are Exercise 1: $r = 0.33$ over 24 months.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rgCin = Inputs.form({
  r: Inputs.range([-0.95, 0.95], {value: 0.33, step: 0.01, label: html`Correlation <i style="text-transform: none">r</i>`}),
  n: Inputs.range([5, 200], {value: 24, step: 1, label: html`Sample size <i style="text-transform: none">n</i>`}),
  alt: Inputs.radio(["ρ > 0", "ρ < 0", "ρ ≠ 0"], {value: "ρ > 0", label: "Alternative"}),
  alpha: Inputs.radio(["10%", "5%", "1%"], {value: "5%", label: html`Level <i style="text-transform: none">α</i>`})
}, {template: ins => html`<div class="rg-dials">${ins.r}${ins.n}</div><div class="rg-dials rg-dials-2">${ins.alt}${ins.alpha}</div>`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {r, n, alt} = rgCin, df = n - 2, a = parseFloat(rgCin.alpha) / 100;
  const t = r * Math.sqrt(df) / Math.sqrt(1 - r * r);
  const crit = clInv(x => clTcdf(x, df))(alt === "ρ ≠ 0" ? 1 - a / 2 : 1 - a);
  const p = alt === "ρ > 0" ? 1 - clTcdf(t, df) : alt === "ρ < 0" ? clTcdf(t, df) : rgP2(t, df);
  const inR = x => alt === "ρ > 0" ? x >= crit : alt === "ρ < 0" ? x <= -crit : Math.abs(x) >= crit;
  const reject = inR(t);
  const dens = x => Math.exp(clLgam((df + 1) / 2) - clLgam(df / 2) - 0.5 * Math.log(df * Math.PI) - (df + 1) / 2 * Math.log(1 + x * x / df));
  const xs = d3.range(-6, 6.001, 0.02).map(x => ({x, y: dens(x)}));
  const cuts = alt === "ρ > 0" ? [crit] : alt === "ρ < 0" ? [-crit] : [-crit, crit];
  const tc = Math.max(-6, Math.min(6, t));
  const chart = Plot.plot({
    width: 1000, height: 250, marginLeft: 12, marginRight: 12, marginBottom: 28, marginTop: 42, style: rgStyle,
    x: {domain: [-6, 6], label: null, tickSize: 4},
    y: {axis: null, domain: [0, 0.42], insetTop: 18},
    marks: [
      Plot.areaY(xs, {x: "x", y: "y", fill: PPAL.dim, fillOpacity: 0.3}),
      Plot.areaY(xs, {x: "x", y: d => inR(d.x) ? d.y : NaN, fill: PPAL.brick, fillOpacity: 0.45}),
      Plot.line(xs, {x: "x", y: "y", stroke: PPAL.soft, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleX(cuts, {stroke: PPAL.brick, strokeWidth: 1.5, strokeDasharray: "5 4"}),
      Plot.ruleX([tc], {stroke: PPAL.orange, strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.text([tc], {x: d => d, y: 0.36, text: () => `t = ${rgN(t, 2)}${Math.abs(t) > 6 ? " (off the axis)" : ""}`, dx: tc > 3 ? -8 : 8,
        textAnchor: tc > 3 ? "end" : "start", fill: PPAL.orange, fontWeight: 700, fontSize: 16, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 6}),
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: PPAL.dim}),
      rgTitle(`Student's t with ${df} degrees of freedom; the red tail is the rejection region`)
    ]
  });
  const word = {"ρ > 0": "greater than zero", "ρ < 0": "less than zero", "ρ ≠ 0": "different from zero"}[alt];
  return html`${chart}
  <div class="ojs-eq rg-stats">
    <span>t = <span class="rate">${rgN(t, 4)}</span></span>
    <span>Critical value ${alt === "ρ ≠ 0" ? "±" : alt === "ρ < 0" ? "−" : ""}${rgN(crit, 4)}</span>
    <span>${rgPeq(p)}</span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb">${reject
    ? html`The statistic t = ${rgN(t, 2)} falls in the rejection region, so we <b>reject H₀</b> at the ${rgCin.alpha} level: the correlation is ${word} (${rgPeq(p)}).`
    : html`The statistic t = ${rgN(t, 2)} is not in the rejection region, so we <b>fail to reject H₀</b> at the ${rgCin.alpha} level (${rgPeq(p)}). A correlation of ${rgN(r, 2)} from only ${n} pairs could be chance.`}</div>`;
}
```

## Finding the Least-Squares Line {.ojs-slide #ls-fit}

::: {.lede-min}
Each line leaves residuals $e_i = y_i - \hat y_i$. Least squares picks the line with the smallest $\text{RSS} = \sum e_i^2$ (ISLR Figures 3.1 and 3.2). Find it with the sliders.
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rgLin = Inputs.form({
  b0: Inputs.range([5, 9], {value: 8.5, step: 0.01, label: html`Intercept <i style="text-transform: none">β₀</i>`}),
  b1: Inputs.range([0.03, 0.065], {value: 0.035, step: 0.0005, label: html`Slope <i style="text-transform: none">β₁</i>`})
}, {template: ins => html`<div class="rg-dials">${ins.b0}${ins.b1}</div>`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// RSS as a quadratic in (b0, b1), from six sums: the contour panel samples it
// thousands of times per redraw, so it must not loop over the 200 markets.
rgSums = {
  const x = rgCol("TV"), y = rgCol("Sales"), s = f => x.reduce((a, _, i) => a + f(x[i], y[i]), 0);
  return {n: x.length, sx: s(u => u), sy: s((u, v) => v), sxx: s(u => u * u), sxy: s((u, v) => u * v), syy: s((u, v) => v * v)};
}
rgRSS = (b0, b1) => { const S = rgSums;
  return S.syy - 2 * b0 * S.sy - 2 * b1 * S.sxy + S.n * b0 * b0 + 2 * b0 * b1 * S.sx + b1 * b1 * S.sxx; }
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {b0, b1} = rgLin, rss = rgRSS(b0, b1), min = rgTV.rss;
  const scatter = Plot.plot({
    width: 500, height: 270, marginLeft: 36, marginBottom: 28, marginTop: 42, style: rgStyle,
    x: {domain: [0, 300], label: null, tickSize: 4},
    y: {domain: [0, 28], label: null, ticks: [0, 10, 20], tickSize: 4},
    marks: [
      Plot.link(rgAd, {x1: "TV", x2: "TV", y1: "Sales", y2: d => b0 + b1 * d.TV, stroke: PPAL.brick, strokeOpacity: 0.55, strokeWidth: 1.2}),
      Plot.dot(rgAd, {x: "TV", y: "Sales", r: 3, fill: PPAL.soft, fillOpacity: 0.6}),
      Plot.line([0, 300], {x: d => d, y: d => b0 + b1 * d, stroke: PPAL.orange, strokeWidth: 3}),
      rgTitle("Your line and its residuals")
    ]
  });
  const contour = Plot.plot({
    width: 480, height: 270, marginLeft: 64, marginBottom: 40, marginTop: 42, style: rgStyle,
    x: {domain: [5, 9], label: "Intercept β₀", labelAnchor: "center", labelArrow: "none", tickSize: 4},
    y: {domain: [0.03, 0.065], label: "Slope β₁", labelAnchor: "center", labelArrow: "none", tickSize: 4, ticks: 4},
    marks: [
      Plot.contour({x1: 5, x2: 9, y1: 0.03, y2: 0.065, value: rgRSS, pixelSize: 3,
        thresholds: [2150, 2200, 2300, 2500, 3000, 4000, 6000, 10000, 16000], stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeOpacity: 0.35, fill: "none"}),
      Plot.dot([rgTV], {x: "b0", y: "b1", symbol: "plus", r: 7, stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot([rgLin], {x: "b0", y: "b1", r: 6, fill: PPAL.orange, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
      rgTitle("RSS for every intercept and slope")
    ]
  });
  const over = rss / min - 1;
  return html`<div class="cr-row">${scatter}${contour}</div>
  <div class="ojs-eq rg-stats">
    <span>Your RSS = <span class="rate">${rgN(rss, 1)}</span></span>
    <span>Least-squares RSS = <span class="cl-navy">${rgN(min, 1)}</span> <span class="na-note">at (${rgN(rgTV.b0)}, ${rgN(rgTV.b1)})</span></span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb ${over < 0.005 ? "quiz-ok" : ""}">${over < 0.005
    ? html`Within 0.5% of the minimum: this is the least-squares line, intercept ${rgN(rgTV.b0, 2)} and slope ${rgN(rgTV.b1)}. No other line leaves a smaller total of squared residuals.`
    : html`Your RSS is <b>${(100 * over).toFixed(1)}% above</b> the minimum. Move the orange dot towards the navy cross: the contours are levels of RSS, and the valley is long and narrow because a steeper slope can be traded for a lower intercept.`}</div>`;
}
```

## The Least-Squares Estimates {.ojs-slide #ls-formula}

::: {.lede-min}
Setting the derivatives of RSS to zero gives the line in closed form. Pick the data, follow the working, then predict.
:::

$$\hat\beta_1 = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar x)(y_i - \bar y)}{\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \bar x)^2}, \qquad \hat\beta_0 = \bar y - \hat\beta_1 \bar x$$

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Exercises 2 and 3 of the beamer Seminar 7, beside ISLR's sales on TV.
rgSets = ({
  "Advertising: sales on TV": {x: rgCol("TV"), y: rgCol("Sales"), lo: 0, hi: 400, x0: 100, step: 1,
    say: b1 => `Each extra $1,000 of TV budget goes with ${(1000 * b1).toFixed(1)} more units sold.`},
  "Exercise 2: Y on X": {x: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7], y: [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128], lo: 0, hi: 10, x0: 5, step: 0.5,
    say: b1 => `A one-unit increase in X goes with an increase of ${rgN(b1, 2)} in Y.`},
  "Exercise 3: cost of debt on sales": {x: [15, 4, 12, 17, 13, 3, 5, 1, 14, 1, 6, 9, 8, 2, 2],
    y: [2, 6, 3, 2, 4, 7, 9, 14, 3, 7, 4, 6, 7, 12, 11], lo: 0, hi: 25, x0: 10, step: 0.5,
    say: b1 => `Each extra £1 million of sales goes with a ${rgN(-b1, 2)} percentage-point lower cost of debt.`}
})
viewof rgFset = Inputs.radio(Object.keys(rgSets), {value: "Advertising: sales on TV", label: "Data"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rgFx0 = Inputs.range([rgSets[rgFset].lo, rgSets[rgFset].hi], {value: rgSets[rgFset].x0, step: rgSets[rgFset].step, label: html`Predict at <i style="text-transform: none">x</i>`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const D = rgSets[rgFset], f = rgSimple(D.x, D.y), yhat = f.b0 + f.b1 * rgFx0;
  const lo = d3.min(D.x), hi = d3.max(D.x), inside = rgFx0 >= lo && rgFx0 <= hi;
  const bar = v => html`<span class="cl-bar">${v}</span>`, hat = v => html`<span class="rg-hat">${v}</span>`;
  return html`<div class="ojs-eq cr-eqs rg-eqs">
    <span>${bar("x")}, ${bar("y")}</span><span>= ${rgN(f.mx)}, ${rgN(f.my)}</span>
    <span>${hat("β")}₁</span><span>= ${rgN(f.sxy, 2)} / ${rgN(f.sxx, 2)} = <span class="cl-navy">${rgN(f.b1)}</span></span>
    <span>${hat("β")}₀</span><span>= ${rgN(f.my)} − ${rgNp(f.b1)} × ${rgN(f.mx)} = <span class="cl-navy">${rgN(f.b0)}</span></span>
    <span>${hat("y")}</span><span>= ${rgN(f.b0)} + ${rgNp(f.b1)} × ${rgFx0} = <span class="${inside ? "rate" : "miss"}">${rgN(yhat)}</span></span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb ${inside ? "" : "quiz-no"}">${D.say(f.b1)} ${inside
    ? html`At x = ${rgFx0}, inside the data's range ${lo} to ${hi}, the line predicts <b>${rgN(yhat, 2)}</b>.`
    : html`But x = ${rgFx0} lies outside the data's range ${lo} to ${hi}: predicting there is <b>extrapolation</b>, and nothing in the data says the line still holds.`}</div>`;
}
```

## How Accurate Is the Slope? {.ojs-slide #ls-accuracy}

::: {.lede-min}
Resample the 200 markets with replacement and refit. The spread of the resampled slopes is what $\text{SE}(\hat\beta_1)$ measures (ISLR Figure 3.3, Table 3.1).
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rgBin = Inputs.form({
  c: Inputs.range([0, 0.06], {value: 0, step: 0.001, label: html`Test H₀: <i style="text-transform: none">β₁</i> =`}),
  again: Inputs.button("New resamples")
}, {template: ins => html`<div class="rg-dials">${ins.c}${ins.again}</div>`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// 1,000 bootstrap resamples, seeded from the button so moving the null value
// keeps the same resamples. Their sd of the slope lands near the formula SE
// (about 0.0028 against 0.0027).
rgBoot = {
  const rnd = d3.randomLcg(((rgBin.again + 1) * 0.6180339887) % 1), x = rgCol("TV"), y = rgCol("Sales");
  const n = x.length, bx = new Array(n), by = new Array(n);
  return Array.from({length: 1000}, () => {
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { const j = Math.floor(rnd() * n); bx[i] = x[j]; by[i] = y[j]; }
    const f = rgSimple(bx, by);
    return {b0: f.b0, b1: f.b1};
  });
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const f = rgTV, c = rgBin.c, lo = f.b1 - 2 * f.se1, hi = f.b1 + 2 * f.se1;
  const t = (f.b1 - c) / f.se1, p = rgP2(t, f.n - 2), inside = c >= lo && c <= hi;
  const lines = Plot.plot({
    width: 490, height: 250, marginLeft: 36, marginBottom: 28, marginTop: 42, style: rgStyle,
    x: {domain: [0, 300], label: null, tickSize: 4},
    y: {domain: [0, 28], label: null, ticks: [0, 10, 20], tickSize: 4},
    marks: [
      Plot.dot(rgAd, {x: "TV", y: "Sales", r: 2.5, fill: PPAL.soft, fillOpacity: 0.35}),
      Plot.link(rgBoot.slice(0, 100), {x1: () => 0, x2: () => 300, y1: d => d.b0, y2: d => d.b0 + 300 * d.b1, stroke: "#9FB6CC", strokeOpacity: 0.6}),
      Plot.line([0, 300], {x: d => d, y: d => f.b0 + f.b1 * d, stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeWidth: 3}),
      rgTitle("A hundred of the 1,000 resampled lines")
    ]
  });
  const hist = Plot.plot({
    width: 490, height: 250, marginLeft: 12, marginBottom: 28, marginTop: 42, style: rgStyle,
    x: {domain: [-0.002, 0.062], label: null, tickSize: 4, ticks: [0, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06]},
    y: {axis: null, insetTop: 18},
    marks: [
      Plot.rectY(rgBoot, Plot.binX({y: "count"}, {x: "b1", thresholds: d3.range(-0.002, 0.0621, 0.0005), fill: "#9FB6CC"})),
      Plot.ruleX([lo, hi], {stroke: PPAL.navy, strokeWidth: 2, strokeDasharray: "5 4"}),
      Plot.ruleX([c], {stroke: PPAL.orange, strokeWidth: 3}),
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: PPAL.dim}),
      rgTitle("Slopes of the 1,000 resamples")
    ]
  });
  const sdBoot = d3.deviation(rgBoot, d => d.b1);
  return html`<div class="cr-row">${lines}${hist}</div>
  <div class="ojs-eq rg-stats">
    <span>SE = <span class="cl-navy">${rgN(f.se1, 5)}</span> <span class="na-note">(resampled sd ${rgN(sdBoot, 5)})</span></span>
    <span>95% CI = [${rgN(lo)}, ${rgN(hi)}]</span>
    <span>t = <span class="rate">${rgN(t, 2)}</span></span>
    <span>${rgPeq(p)}</span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb">${inside
    ? html`The value ${c} lies inside the interval β̂₁ ± 2·SE, so the test keeps it: t = ${rgN(t, 2)}, ${rgPeq(p)}. The interval is the set of null values the test does not reject at 5%.`
    : html`The value ${c} lies outside the interval β̂₁ ± 2·SE, so we <b>reject H₀</b>: t = (${rgN(f.b1, 5)} − ${c}) / ${rgN(f.se1, 5)} = ${rgN(t, 2)}, ${rgPeq(p)}.${c === 0 ? " TV advertising is related to sales, as in ISLR Table 3.1." : ""}`}</div>`;
}
```

## How Well Does the Line Fit? {.qcard-slide #fit-quality}

::: {.lede-min}
Three numbers summarise the fit of sales on TV (ISLR 3.1.3). The first is in the units of $y$; the other two are shares of the variation in $y$.
:::

:::: {.prop-grid}

::: {.prop-card .prop-rse .fragment}
[Residual standard error]{.prop-name}

[$\text{RSE} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\text{RSS}}{n-2}}$]{.prop-math}

[Sales miss the line by about ${rgN(rgTV.rse, 2)} thousand units, ${(100 * rgTV.rse / rgTV.my).toFixed(0)}% of average sales.]{.prop-q}
:::

::: {.prop-card .prop-r2 .fragment}
[R²]{.prop-name}

[$R^2 = 1 - \dfrac{\text{RSS}}{\text{TSS}}$]{.prop-math}

[TV explains ${(100 * rgTV.r2).toFixed(1)}% of the variation in sales.]{.prop-q}
:::

::: {.prop-card .prop-adj .fragment}
[Adjusted R²]{.prop-name}

[$\bar R^2 = 1 - \dfrac{\text{RSS}/(n-k-1)}{\text{TSS}/(n-1)}$]{.prop-math}

[Equal to ${rgN(rgTV.adj, 3)} here. It charges for each of the $k$ predictors, so use it to compare models.]{.prop-q}
:::

::::

::: {.slide-footer .fragment}
In simple regression $R^2 = r^2$: the correlation of sales and TV is ${rgN(rgTV.r, 3)}, and ${rgN(rgTV.r, 3)}² = ${rgN(rgTV.r2, 3)}. Adding a predictor never lowers $R^2$, which is why adjusted $R^2$ is the fair comparison.
:::

## Simple Versus Multiple Regression {.ojs-slide #multi-reg}

::: {.lede-min}
Tick the media to include. Each coefficient is the change in sales per $1,000 on that medium, holding the other ticked media fixed (ISLR 3.2).
:::

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof rgMx = Inputs.checkbox(["TV", "Radio", "Newspaper"], {value: ["TV", "Radio", "Newspaper"], label: "Predictors"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const vars = ["TV", "Radio", "Newspaper"].filter(v => rgMx.includes(v));
  const cols = ["TV", "Radio", "Newspaper", "Sales"];
  const cor = (a, b) => rgSimple(rgCol(a), rgCol(b)).r;
  const corTable = html`<table class="rg-table rg-cor">
    <thead><tr><th></th>${cols.map(c => html`<th>${c}</th>`)}</tr></thead>
    <tbody>${cols.map(a => html`<tr><th>${a}</th>${cols.map(b => html`<td class=${(a === "Radio" && b === "Newspaper") || (a === "Newspaper" && b === "Radio") ? "ct-top" : ""}>${rgN(cor(a, b), 2)}</td>`)}</tr>`)}</tbody>
  </table>`;
  if (!vars.length) return html`<div class="rg-row"><div class="quiz-fb">Tick at least one medium to fit a model.</div>${corTable}</div>`;
  const m = rgOls(vars), pF = rgFp(m.F, m.k - 1, m.df);
  const coef = html`<table class="rg-table">
    <thead><tr><th></th><th>Coefficient</th><th>Std. error</th><th>t</th><th>p-value</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>${m.names.map((nm, i) => html`<tr class=${nm === "Newspaper" ? "rg-news" : ""}><th>${nm}</th><td>${rgN(m.b[i])}</td><td>${rgN(m.se[i])}</td><td>${rgN(m.t[i], 2)}</td><td>${rgPfmt(rgP2(m.t[i], m.df))}</td></tr>`)}</tbody>
  </table>`;
  const ni = m.names.indexOf("Newspaper"), np = ni > 0 ? rgP2(m.t[ni], m.df) : null;
  const m2 = ni < 0 ? rgOls([...vars, "Newspaper"]) : null;
  const say = ni < 0
    ? html`F = ${rgN(m.F, 1)} (${rgPeq(pF)}): at least one ticked medium is related to sales. Adding newspaper would raise R² from ${rgN(m.r2, 5)} to ${rgN(m2.r2, 5)}, but ${m2.adj < m.adj ? "lower" : "raise"} adjusted R² from ${rgN(m.adj, 5)} to ${rgN(m2.adj, 5)}.`
    : vars.includes("Radio")
      ? html`Holding radio${vars.includes("TV") ? " and TV" : ""} fixed, newspaper's coefficient is <b>${rgN(m.b[ni])}</b> (${rgPeq(np)}): no effect of its own. On its own it looked useful only because markets that spend on radio also spend on newspapers (r = ${rgN(cor("Radio", "Newspaper"), 2)}).`
      : html`Without radio, newspaper's coefficient is <b>${rgN(m.b[ni])}</b> (${rgPeq(np)}). It picks up radio's effect, because the two budgets are correlated (r = ${rgN(cor("Radio", "Newspaper"), 2)}): this is <b>omitted variable bias</b>. Tick radio to see it vanish.`;
  return html`<div class="rg-row">${coef}${corTable}</div>
  <div class="ojs-eq rg-stats">
    <span>R² = ${rgN(m.r2, 3)}</span>
    <span>Adjusted R² = ${rgN(m.adj, 3)}</span>
    <span>RSE = ${rgN(m.rse, 2)}</span>
    <span>F = <span class="cl-navy">${rgN(m.F, 1)}</span> <span class="na-note">(${rgPeq(pF)})</span></span>
  </div>
  <div class="quiz-fb">${say}</div>`;
}
```
